criteria.text: Confirmed diagnosis of phenylketonuria (PKU); the closed indication is adult PKU with uncontrolled Phe >600 µmol/L on existing management (approval criterion 2).
Patient is 18 years of age or older (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a metabolic specialist (approval criterion 3).
Both prescriber and patient are enrolled in the REMS program (approval criterion 3).
Baseline phenylalanine levels have been documented (approval criterion 4).
Patient is actively on a phenylalanine restricted diet (approval criterion 5).
Uncontrolled blood phenylalanine >600 µmol/L on existing management (e.g. Kuvan agents; approval criterion 6).
Phenylalanine levels are monitored and recorded through therapy (approval criterion 7).
Auto-injectable epinephrine prescribed and patient trained on proper use (approval criterion 8).
Patient is not concomitantly using Kuvan agents with Palynziq (denial criterion 7).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Palynziq (pegvaliase-pqpz), a phenylalanine-metabolizing enzyme for adult PKU. Version 1; Original 12/7/2018; Approval 1/18/19; Effective 3/11/19.

Encoded: closed confirmed PKU indication, age ≥18, approval criteria 1-8, and denial criterion 7 (concomitant Kuvan). Other denials mirror approval gates. Specialty and both-party REMS enrollment are separate required attestations.

Existing management (e.g. Kuvan agents) is included in the uncontrolled Phe >600 µmol/L attestation; no separate Kuvan failure requirement is imposed. Prior management and concomitant Kuvan use are distinct.

Black Box Warning (notes only): anaphylaxis can occur at any time during treatment. Give the initial dose under healthcare provider supervision with capacity to manage anaphylaxis and observe for at least 60 minutes. Before self-injection, confirm self-administration competency and patient/observer ability to recognize anaphylaxis and administer epinephrine.

Cautions (notes only): before the first dose instruct the patient and observer, if applicable, on epinephrine use; seek immediate medical care after use. Carry auto-injectable epinephrine at all times during treatment.
Monitoring schedule (notes only): obtain blood Phe every 4 weeks until maintenance dosage is established, then periodically.

Duration (notes only): initial approval 3 months; reauthorization up to 6 months with continued improvement measured by ≥20% reduction from pre-treatment baseline OR Phe <600 µmol/L, and no toxicities or adverse reactions.
Quantity (notes only): up to 40 mg/day (2 syringes max daily); 60 syringes/month. max_units is null; dosing and quantity are not evaluated.

Documentation verification, monitoring schedule, administration and safety cautions, duration, reauthorization response and tolerability, dosing, and quantity limits require manual review; this pack remains partial.
